components.name: Lane Diff
components.description: A split diff of each changed lane: now at the left, after the change at the right. Added lines on diff-add, removed on diff-remove, changed words on the word tones, + and − in the diff inks, → lane for a moved task, folded unchanged runs. A new lane is a box with an ink border and a NEW LANE tag under the right side.

narrative.overview: Tenface is a ledger that the owner reads in a few seconds. Every project, lane, task and step is written down in warm, paper-like Sepia tones, in tables and trees that read like a well-kept book. The page does not glow or decorate. Its one color, a blood red, says "this runs now". What the agents ask the owner does not sit on the page. Each question belongs to the agent that asked it: the planner of the project (P) or the babysitter of a lane (B). The agent is a ring that shows its context use, and a small card on the ring counts its open questions. Tap the ring and its card lists the questions. The owner answers in that agent's chat, for example "Q12 ok". The surface is light Sepia, also on a device set to dark. The dark Sepia twins live under data-theme="dark"; until a real theme switch exists, ?theme=dark or ?theme=light in the URL sets it. There is no accent color. Shapes follow Apple's current capsule forms without the glass. The phone answers "what now"; the desktop shows project, lane and task side by side.
keyCharacteristics: Done is a filled gray square, running a filled red square, waiting an empty outline; these marks draw the tree. A project row shows only a red "running", a lane row a red "N tasks running"; the lane head shows all counts in words over a capsule bar.
A lane tree and a question list read as tables: a line number, the content, and a short column at the right.
Red means running and nothing else; a question is a count on the asking agent's ring. The one exception is the lane diff, which uses git's green and red.
Every question has an id (Q12) that is unique across the whole system.
Ink marks where the owner is: the current tab, the selected row, the selected desktop lane.
An error of the whole panel is an ink strip at the top of every screen.
A plan change is read-only; the owner answers it in the planner's chat.
A lane is one tree with lines from root to leaf.

rules.name: The Red Means Running Rule
rules.body: Red marks what runs now and nothing else. No red for a question, an error, a link, a brand or decoration. The diff red is a separate token that lives only inside the lane diff.

rules.name: The No Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no second color. Selection, focus and "current" are shown with ink, weight and tone. The diff green and red are the one exception, because the owner reads a diff in git's colors.

rules.name: The Pick Rule
rules.body: The picked task row in the tree is a Raised Sepia row across the full width of the tree, with a semibold title. The selected lane row in the desktop lanes table rises as a light card: the Lift fill, a 1 px line ring and a soft 2 px / 6 px shadow. The current tab keeps its 1.5 px ink border. The panel has no ink row.

rules.name: The Card Head Rule
rules.body: A card opens with its head on a band: the Card Head line, then the Subject, on a Raised Sepia band that runs to the card edges and top corners (project card, lane card, task card, agent card, task sheet). A level below is never heavier than the level above. A Card Head outside a card has no band.

rules.name: The Project Holds Rule
rules.body: On the desktop the project card holds the page: a full-width band (Project · sample, red running, back arrow, P ring), the lanes list without a frame, and the lane and task cards inside in Lift white, their bands on one row with the same height. The task card keeps its band when nothing is picked: Task, No task selected. On the phone each level is its own page with a back link naming the level above.

rules.name: The Sizes Rule
rules.body: Only 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 20 and 28 px exist: 13 px for table lines (tree, diff, questions), 11 px only for a tag or a diff head, and the 9 px mark inside a small agent icon. A long title wraps; it is never cut.

rules.name: The Last Pick Rule
rules.body: The desktop detail column shows the last pick. A plan change spans the lane and task columns and becomes the main content. The picked task stays a Raised Sepia row; the selected lane row is a lifted card while its task is shown, and only a 2 px ink outline while a plan change is shown.

rules.name: The Error Rule
rules.body: An error of the whole panel is an ink strip at the top of every screen; an error of one thing stays in place; a button only when the owner's action fixes it.

rules.name: The Offline Rule
rules.body: Offline, the panel shows the last known state under the strip: the running notes, the lane progress and the ring keep their last colors, and the strip alone says the panel is offline. Only the running node turns into a 2 px gray outline and its step cell turns muted with a gray outline.

rules.name: The Flat Unless Floating Rule
rules.body: No shadow on anything that lies in the page; only the nav, the agent ring, the agent card and the task sheet float. On the phone, behind an open agent card or the task sheet, the page and the nav are dimmed with ink at 32%.

dos: Do show in a row only what runs: "running" for a project, "N tasks running" for a lane; the lane head gives all three counts.
Do put a question in the card of the agent that asked it, with its id and the waiting time.
Do close a question when the owner answers it in the chat: a hook in the asking agent's session (the babysitter's or the planner's) tells the server, and the row leaves the card.
Do show the agent on every lane and project page, and let the owner drag it out of the way.
Do show a plan change before it is applied, as a split lane diff: + and − lines, the changed words marked, and → lane for a task that moves.
Do give every focusable element a 2 px ink focus ring with a 2 px offset.
Do write times as "11:20" for today and "Nov 13, 20:30" for another day.
donts: Don't use red for a question, an error or anything that does not run.
Don't add an accent color, a gradient, glass, blur or a second attention color.
Don't put a list of questions on a page; questions live in the agent card.
Don't write a state word next to an agent; the ring says it.
Don't add Approve or Reject to a plan change.
Don't use a font size outside 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 20 and 28 px, or cut a title with "…".
Don't draw drag handles or drop zones for tasks; the tree is never edited by hand.
Don't use real client, project or task names in designs or code; sample data is made up.
Don't use the diff green or red outside a lane diff.
